blocks.text: Single inheritance tab hoti hai jab child class (subclass) sirf aik parent class (superclass) se attributes aur methods leti hai. Yeh Python mein inheritance ki sab se bunyadi shakal hai; child class parent ke behaviour ko barha ya badal sakti hai, is se code dobara istemal hota hai (Figure 3.3).

blocks.alt: Single inheritance: Child Class ka dabba Parent Class ke neeche hai; dono aik lakeer se jure hain jis ka khokhla (hollow) teer ka sira Parent Class par hai.
blocks.caption: Figure 3.3: Single Inheritance (kitab ki Figure 3.3 ke mutabiq asal khaaka).

blocks.title: Diagram ko samjhein
blocks.text: Teer child class se parent class ki taraf jata hai aur us ka khokhla (hollow) sira parent par hai. Matlab: child parent se inherit karti hai, yani parent ke attributes aur methods le leti hai. Neeche wali misal mein Animal parent hai aur Dog child.
Is misal mein Dog class Animal ki bunyadi functionality le leti hai aur apna khaas kaam bhi shamil karti hai.

Buddy is eating.
Buddy says Woof!
blocks.caption: Output (program chala kar)

blocks.title: Code Explanation (Wazahat)
blocks.text:
"#" se shuru hone wali lines comments hain; Python inhein nahi chalata.
"class Animal:": parent class (superclass). __init__ naam (name) rakhta hai; eat() print karta hai "<naam> is eating.". f-string (f"...") mein {self.name} ki jagah naam aa jata hai.
"class Dog(Animal):": brackets mein Animal likhne ka matlab hai ke Dog, Animal se inherit karti hai: Animal ka __init__ aur eat() Dog ko mil jate hain. Dog apna naya method bark() bhi jorti hai.
"my_dog = Dog(\"Buddy\")": Dog ka object bana. Dog ka apna __init__ nahi, is liye Animal wala __init__ chala aur name = "Buddy" hua.
"my_dog.eat()": yeh method parent (Animal) se aaya. "my_dog.bark()": yeh child (Dog) ka apna method hai.
Output: "Buddy is eating." aur "Buddy says Woof!" (book ke comments mein bhi yahi likha hai).
Khud try karein: "Buddy" ki jagah "Moti" likhein; dono lines mein naya naam aayega.

blocks.title: Tidbit (dilchasp baat)
blocks.text: self maujooda object ka hawala (reference) hai; Python ise instance methods ko khud bhejta hai.

items: Parent Class (Base Class): woh class jis ki properties inherit hoti hain. Oopar wali misal mein Animal parent class hai.
Child Class (Derived Class): woh class jo parent se inherit karti hai. Is ko banate waqt parent ka naam brackets mein likha jata hai: class Child(Parent):.
Method Overriding: child class parent mein pehle se maujood method ka apna version de sakti hai. Parent wala version call karne ke liye super() function istemal hota hai.

blocks.text: Method Overriding aur super() ki misal (kitab mein nahi): Puppy class Dog se inherit karti hai, apna eat() deti hai, aur us ke andar super().eat() se pehle parent wala eat() chalati hai. name badal kar Run karein.

blocks.title: Code Explanation (Wazahat)
blocks.text:
"name = \"Moti\"": puppy ka naam.
Animal aur Dog wahi classes hain jo kitab ki misal mein hain.
"class Puppy(Dog):": Puppy, Dog se inherit karti hai (aur Dog, Animal se).
"def eat(self):" Puppy ke andar: parent ke eat() ko override karta hai, yani Puppy ka apna eat().
"super().eat()": super() parent class ki taraf ishara hai; yeh pehle parent wala eat() chalata hai ("Moti is eating."), phir agli line "Moti wants more milk." print karti hai.
"p.bark()": bark() Dog se inherit hua.
Output: teen lines: "Moti is eating.", "Moti wants more milk." aur "Moti says Woof!".
Khud try karein: super().eat() wali line hata kar Run karein: "Moti is eating." nahi aayega, kyun ke ab sirf Puppy ka apna eat() chalta hai.

items: Single inheritance: ek child, ek parent (Dog(Animal)).
Parent = base class, child = derived class: class Child(Parent):.
Method overriding: child apna version deti hai; super() parent ka version chalata hai.
